source.quote: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where a road Goldilocks is carving his way through Azeroth one zone at a time. And our most recent unlock, Duskwood, is already proving itself to be a pretty solid zone with silk finally coming in, housing crafts moving, and some more profitable farms revealing themselves every day. Let's dive a little deeper. Because we ended last episode only about 90,000 gold short of the next token. So, if we get some good gold here this week, we could be rolling a new zone pretty soon. So travelers, let's get back into Deskwood and keep the momentum rolling. Now, with every new zone unlock, there are a few types of farms that just jump to the top of my list of what I want to find. Now, of course, one type of farm in particular is specifically because we rolled a rogue, not the meta druid gold farmer. So, let's see what we can find pickpocketing in Duskwood. Now, there are plenty of humanoids across Duskwood to test. And after looking over a few of the pickpocket loot tables on Wowhead, I think we might be in for a treat because nearly every humanoid here can drop a battered junk boxes. So, I think the plan is simple. We need to figure out who the best humanoid to pickpocket is and fill up a bank tab of battered junk boxes or about a hundred and see if it's actually worth farming these because I'm already having a few flashbacks to burning steps with the junk boxes there.

source.quote: But maybe we can hope for better luck in Duskwood. What should we hit? Well, there are Nightbane Wargan running around Duskwood. And these were my first thought after Wargan became a playable race. You can no longer actually skin them in game, which means we can't double dip with farming junk boxes and medium leather. I mean, they do have some solid drops on their loot tables, but let's see what else we can find. And after some research, up north, there are fedded corpses. These guys do have junk boxes on their pickpocket tables, and they actually have an ultra rare drop on their loot tables. the Black Metal Great Sword. This is a 0.02% drop rate, so about 1 in 5,000, but it has a market value between 50k and 100k.

source.quote: We also didn't have a reliable source for one of the ores required to level blacksmithing from 155 to 200, iron ore. And Duskwood solves that. Well, kind of. So, iron ore does spawn here in Duskwood, but it's rare and spread out. And compared to a zone like Strangle Thorn Veil, where iron is everywhere, Duskwood is mostly just copper and tin with the occasional iron ore node mixed in. The problem is to level up blacksmithing properly, we're going to need roughly 420 iron ore, and some of that will be smelted into iron bars with the other being smelted with coal into steel bars. So, since the nodes are so scarce, I think the best play here is to build a full duskwood mining loop that hits every possible iron ore spawn.

source.quote: There aren't too many of them. If we work around them a little bit, we can actually form a decent route. Now, sometimes these nodes do spawn as copper and tin, but every time we mine them, they might respawn as iron. It's not perfect, but given our zone restrictions, it is the best option we have. So, while we're grinding iron ore on our route, which by the way, if you're wondering, we are using the routes add-on in game to build this route. Just makes it way easier to follow it. But, let's talk about why we actually want to level blocks something in the first place. And this is where things get pretty interesting. Because ultimately, what we're going to have to do makes the iron ore grind feel like a little tip of the iceberg. For starters, most blacksmithing crafts from levels 1 to 240, the ones we're going to be leveling up with, don't really have much of a profit, unless you're already sitting on some rare recipes. At this point in the challenge, if a green item isn't selling for more than 1,000 gold, it's honestly not worth the reposting time. Our transmog character now has over 700 auctions, and posting those every day already takes a good amount of time. This changes at level 240 blacksmithing. That's the break point and the starters because it does unlock classic housing decor crafts. And while Blacksmithing does have multiple decor recipes, only one of them is actually possible within our currently unlocked zones. And the other, well, it requires Arcanite bars, which we're still gated on. But here's the thing, travelers. 240 and housing crafts is just a stepping stone. The real gold and the real grind for Goldie is going to start at 300. But anyways, before we get ahead of ourselves here, let's finish off these last levels with the iron we farmed. The iron ore grind, all things considered, isn't all too bad. We've done far crazier ore farms in the series, aside from a couple missing reagents like mage and mithil.

And if we add it all up, the materials that we farmed and used for crafting, which we then vendored or disenchanted to reach 240 blacksmithing, represent a sunk cost of about 8,262 gold of trade goods. These are items that we could have just sold on the auction house. So, we definitely want to make sure we're at least covering this cost. And the first real profitable craft to do so is the shadow forge sconce. This one does require 10 lumber, pretty cheap on the lumber side, 12 dark iron bars, four lava cores, and two brilliant shards. All things we can technically get, right? Well, almost.

source.quote: Unfortunately for Gloom Rail, accessing it does require defeating the seven. And yeah, Gloom is one of the seven dwarves. The path is open and we can step into the Black Forge. And with that, we can finally smelt dark iron ore. And honestly, travelers, it's times like this on Goldbound. Checkpoints that take months, multiple zone unlocks, long material grinds, and old quest lines finally paying off that really make the Goldbound journey super fun and meaningful for me. Slow progress and unlocks. So, with fresh dark iron ore in our bags, we can officially check off the shadow forge sconce from the crafting list. Now, to be quite honest with you, the real unlocks happen at blacksmithing 300, and we are going to get there this episode. But before we push deeper into mining and blacksmithing, I think it's time Goldie had a little bit of leisure time. And what a better way to take a break than with a bit of fishing. At first glance, it doesn't really seem like Duskwood has much going on from a fishing perspective. We can definitely scout out properly before running it off. And looking at the map, there aren't many obvious water sources inside the zone itself. But there are rivers all around Duskwood bordering Westfall and Elwin. So I think that's as good a spot as any to start. First cast on the Westfall side, a raw bristle whisker catfish, which is a pretty standard Eastern Kingdoms fish and not very valuable. Second cast, a mana potion, unique, but not exactly a gold mine either. And a raw long jaw mud snapper, which we've seen plenty of these in Elwin. Nothing surprising so far. On the mini map though, I do spot sage fish schools on the river. So, let's go check those out. These are the same pools we were farming back in Red Ridge, and we know they can drop watertight trunks and sage fish themselves. Right now, sage fish are sitting around 50 silver to 1 gold each. So, based on that alone, doesn't really feel like something worth farming heavily. And on average, from our red ridge testing, the trunks are worth about 70 gold each with the trade goods and materials inside. Now, what about the waters inside of Duskwood? In the center of the zone, there is the Twilight Grove. In retail, there isn't much going on here besides the Moonwell.

source.quote: And just to confirm, you cannot fish in Moonwells. I did have to test this one. Same thing goes for the Dark Shower Fountain. And you might think I'm crazy for testing this, but hey, maybe no one ever tried it. Plus, the Daron fountain is a fishable water source. Anyways, after scouting all of the south and the rest of Duskwood, I'm only really finding one more real body of water that's actually in Duskwood and is fishable. And honestly, it's a pretty cool spot. So, behind the tower in the northeast of Duskwood is an area called the Beggar's Haunt. And it's home to the rare spawn, the Unknown Soldier, who unfortunately doesn't have much to note on his loot tables. But right beside him is a nice little waterfall fed pool. A really nice little fishing spot in theory, but the fish, yep, more the same. Catfish and snappers. So, just from a pure fishing standpoint, Duskwood is kind of a dud. And just as a side note, I did go on my main and scout up the waterfalls to the source of the waterfall, and there's no other unique fish up there. That being said, we can spice things up a bit for fishing here.
